content: ok let me set the scene — i'm switching the amiko-web backend off prisma. tired of fighting the partial-select types.
what are you moving to?
drizzle. i did a spike last week and the type inference on partial selects is just better. prisma was giving me `unknown` on like every conditional include.
drizzle has its own gotchas, mainly around relational queries. you ok with that tradeoff?
yeah, willing to live with it. type quality matters more to me than the relational ergonomics.
also: writing this down so future-me remembers — error responses across the api follow `{error: {code, message, hint}}`. i keep re-deciding this.
do you want me to remember that as a pattern?
please. it's bitten me twice.
oh and — i'm running the web app on vercel, backend on railway. that's the stack going forward.
random — i tried that dim sum place sasha mentioned. it was fine.
fine as in good or fine as in mid?
mid. har gow was overcooked. not going back.
also — quick aside, what's the weather like in nyc tomorrow?
i don't have live weather. you can check apple weather.
fair. ok back to amiko-web — i'm going to keep prefering pnpm over npm for the monorepo. last week i tried switching to npm for a day and the install times tripled. settled.
and one more rule i want to keep — commit messages focus on the WHY, never on the WHAT. i'm sick of 'updated file.ts' commits.
noted.
did i tell you i lost my keys last week
you mentioned it. did you find them?
yeah, in the laundry. anyway.
tomorrow i'm migrating the user table off prisma. should be straightforward. will report back.
good luck.
one more — i think i'm going to use turborepo for the monorepo dev cache. tried nx, too heavy.
but actually i'm not 100% on that yet. might revisit after the prisma migration.
ok signing off for the night
later
wait one more thing — the slim profile extraction pipeline is timing out on conversations over 80 messages. gemini just bails. i'm going to tail-truncate the input.
the tail is where the actual signal is anyway. people drift into chitchat at the start, then settle on decisions by the end.
makes sense. 80 messages should keep you well under gemini's context too.
yeah confirmed. tail-truncate to 80, that's the rule going forward.
ok really signing off this time
night
what time is it
i don't have a clock. check your menu bar.
fair enough
actually one more — i'm going to standardize on vitest over jest for new test files. jest is fine for legacy but the speed difference is real on the watch loop.
for new files only?
yeah. not migrating the existing jest suite, that's a yak-shave.
OK done. sleeping. for real this time.
night
(came back) realized i didn't decide between turborepo and nx, let me decide now. turborepo. final answer. lighter, faster for our scale, and the remote cache story is cleaner.
got it.
now i'm really gone. bye.
later
did i ever tell you i broke my wrist when i was 12
no but glad to hear you're better
lol yes that was 20 years ago
ok let me actually log off
bye
